report: Friday, 13 November. A quiet day for orders, a weak day for our one holding. The trader placed no orders and nothing filled, so there were no costs today. The only position is Infineon, six shares bought at 50.90 euros on 10 November. It closed at 49.88, down about 4 percent from yesterday's close of 52.11. That fits the chip selloff after the Nvidia CEO exit, which hit the whole sector, not just Infineon. Infineon is now about 2 percent below our entry and about 6 percent above the stop near 46.82. The exit date is 24 November, seven trading days away. The day result is minus 13.41 euros, or minus 0.67 percent. Total result is minus 0.43 percent. One odd thing: yesterday's note showed equity of about 1,005 euros and cash of 692. Today the account shows a 2,000 euro start and cash of 1,692. That looks like a 1,000 euro top-up or a reset of the start value. The day's loss matches the price move, and reconcile says consistent, but we should confirm what changed. The input also had no fresh news or index data, so I cannot say more about the market. One down day says nothing about skill. No trade has closed and no shadow call has scored yet.
questions: The account start moved from about 1,000 to 2,000 euros and cash rose by exactly 1,000. Was this a deliberate top-up or reset, and should the trader size new positions from the new equity?

Our stop is a fixed 8 percent below entry. When a sector-wide shock like the Nvidia CEO exit moves all chips together, should the stop still apply the same way, or should the rule depend on whether the drop is company-specific?
Today's reviewer input had no market or news data, only the account. Should the close job always pass index, sector and theme prices so the review can separate luck from reasoning?
